221.subject: Botany
221.sol: Phosphorus is a major constituent of biological membranes, nucleic acids and cellular energy transfer systems. Many animals also need large quantities of this element to make shells, bones and teeth. The natural reservoir of phosphorus is rock, which contains phosphorus in the form of phosphates. When rocks are weathered, minute amounts of these phosphates dissolve in soil solution and are absorbed by the roots of the plants. Herbivores and other animals obtain this element from plants.

310.text:
Assertion : Vernalization is acceleration of subsquent flowering by low temperature treatment.
Reason : Site of vernalization is apical meristem.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
310.sol: Term vernalization was first given by T.D. Lysenko (1928). In colder countries, there are cereals of 2 physiological types, i.e., winter cereals and spring cereals. Winter cereals are sown in winter and flower in following summer whereas spring cereals are sown in spring and flower in summer. If winter cereal is sown in spring, it shows vegetative growth but does not flower unless it receives low temperature of winter. But winter cereal can be converted into spring cereal by providing artificial low temperature treatment, (i.e., springification.) Some plants requiring low temperature requirement (vernalization) for flowering are Secale cereale (European rye), Triticum vulgare, Brassica oleracea, Beta vulgaris, Apium and Lolium perenne, etc. Site of vernalization is apical meristem or all the meristematic cells. As a result of vernalization, a flowering hormone called "vernalin" is formed (reported by Melchers), but venalin has never been isolated. Once a plant is vernalized, it can be devernalized by exposing the plant to temperature of \(30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\) or above. For establishing vernalization, plant should be kept at \(20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\) for \(4-5\) days.

1997.text:
Assertion : Hormone calcitonin has antagonistic effect to that of parathormone.
Reason : Calcitonin decreases blood calcium level while parathormone increases blood calcium level.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1997.sol: Calcitonin or thyrocalcitonin is secreted by parafollicular cells of thyroid stroma. It retards bone dissolution and stimulates excretion of calcium in urine. Thus, it lowers calcium level in extra cellular fluid (ECF). Parathormone is secreted by chief cells of parathyroid gland and is also known as Collip's hormone. It maintains blood calcium level by increasing its absorption from food in intestine and its reabsorption from nephrons in the kidney. Maintenance of proper calcium level is in fact, a combined function of parathormone and calcitonin. When calcium level falls below normal then parathormone maintains it by promoting its absorption, reabsorption and also by demineralization of bones. When blood calcium level exceeds above normal then calcitonin hormone increases excretion of calcium in the urine.

3346.text:
Which of the following statements are correct for classification of elements?
I. The properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
II. Non-metallic elements are less in number than the metallic elements.
III. The first ionisation energies of elements along a period do not vary in a regular manner.
IV. The ground state electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Pd}(Z=46)$ is $[\mathrm{Kr}] 4 d^8 5 s^2$.
3346.sol:
(I, II) Properties of elements are periodic function of their atomic number. Number of non-metals are less as compared to number of metallic elements.
(III) In periodic table, first ionisation energy of elements along a period do not vary in regular manner due to effective nuclear charge.
(IV) Ground state electronic configuration of $\operatorname{Pd}[Z=46]$ is $[\mathrm{Kr}] 4 d^{10} 5 s^0$.
Hence, IVth statement is incorrect.
Thus, option (b) is correct.

5232.text: A solution is prepared by dissolving $10 \mathrm{ g}$ of a non-volatile solute (molar mass, ' $M^{\prime} \mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) in $360 \mathrm{ g}$ of water. What is the molar mass in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ of solute if the relative lowering of vapour pressure of solution is $5 \times 10^{-3}$ ?
5232.sol:
Given,

Mass of solute $\left(w_B\right)=10 \mathrm{~g}$
Molar mass of solute $\left(M_B\right)=M_B$
Mass of solvent $\left(w_A\right)=360 \mathrm{~g}$
Relative lowering in vapour pressure of solution

=5 $\times$10^{-3}

Molar mass of water $\left(M_A\right)=18 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\because \frac{\Delta p}{p^{{}^{\circ}}}=$ Relative lower in vapour-pressure of solution.

$\frac{\Delta p}{p^{{}^{\circ}}}=\chi_$B \Rightarrow $\frac{n_B}{n_A+n_B}=$5 $\times$10^{-3}

where, $n_A and n_B$ are number of moles of solvent $(A)$ and solute $(B)$ respectively.

$\begin{aligned}$n_A & =$\frac{360}{18}=$20 \\
n_B & =$\frac{w_B}{M_B}=\frac{10}{M_B}$\\
\because \quad 5 $\times$10^{-3} & =\chi_B=$\frac{\frac{10}{M_B}}{20+\frac{10}{M_B}}
\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}$& 5 $\times$10^{-3}=$\frac{\frac{10}{M_B}}{\frac{20 M_B+10}{M_B}}$\\
& 5 $\times$10^{-3}=$\frac{10}{20 M_B+10}$\\
&$\left(20 M_B+10\right) 5 $\times$10^{-3}= 10 \\
& \text{ or, } \quad$20 M_B+10=$\frac{10}{5}$ \times$10^3 \\
& 20 M_B+10=2000 \Rightarrow 20 M_B=1990 \\
& M_B=\frac{1990}{20}$=$99.5 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\end{aligned}Hence, option (b) is$ the correct answer.

10628.text: In a test a student either guesses or copies or knows the answer to answer a multiple choice question with four choices. The probability that he makes a guess is $1 / 3$ and the probability that he copies the answer is $1 / 6$. The probability that his answer is correct, given that he copied it is $1 / 8$. The probability that he knew the answer to the question, given that he answered it correctly is
10628.sol:
Let define the following events:
$\mathrm{E}_1$ : Students gusses the answer to the question.
$\mathrm{E}_2$ : Students copies the answer to the question.
$\mathrm{E}_3$ : Students know the answer to the quesiton.
$\mathrm{E}:$ Answer is correct.
Here, $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_1\right)=\frac{1}{3}, \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_2\right)=\frac{1}{6}\therefore \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_3\right)=1-\left(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}\right)=\frac{1}{2}$
Since, the question is a multiple choice question with four choice. So the probability that the answer is correct when it is gussed, $\Rightarrow P\left(\frac{E}{E_1}\right)=\frac{1}{4}$
Also, the probability that his answer is correct, given that he copied it is $\frac{1}{8} \Rightarrow P\left(\frac{E}{E_2}\right)=\frac{1}{8}$
Moreover, his answer is correct, given he know the answer is sure event, so $\mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{E}_3}\right)=1$
Hence, by Baye's theorem, the required probability is
$\Rightarrow P\left(\frac{E_3}{E}\right)=\frac{P\left(\frac{E}{E_3}\right) P\left(E_3\right)}{P\left(\frac{E}{E_1}\right) P\left(E_1\right)+P\left(\frac{E}{E_2}\right) P\left(E_2\right)+P\left(\frac{E}{E_3}\right) P\left(E_3\right)}\Rightarrow P\left(\frac{E_3}{E}\right)=\frac{1 \times \frac{1}{2}}{\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{8} \times \frac{1}{6}+1 \times \frac{1}{2}}=\frac{24}{29}$

19757.subject: Chemistry
19757.text: In which one of the following pairs does the stability of the monovalent ion increase with respect to the molecule, while the magnetic character remains the same for both?
19757.sol:
Stability increases when an electron is removed from an antibonding MO (bond order increases). Magnetic character remains the same if both species have the same type (both paramagnetic or both diamagnetic).

(1) $N_2/N_2^+$: $N_2$ — electron removed from bonding $\sigma 2p_z$, BO decreases $3 \to 2.5$. Also $N_2$ is diamagnetic but $N_2^+$ is paramagnetic. Fails both conditions.

(2) $O_2/O_2^+$: $O_2$ — highest occupied MOs are antibonding $\pi^*2p$, BO $= 2$, paramagnetic (2 unpaired electrons). $O_2^+$ — electron removed from $\pi^*$, BO $= 2.5$ (stability increases), 1 unpaired electron — still paramagnetic. Satisfies both conditions.

(3) $C_2/C_2^+$: Electron removed from bonding $\pi 2p$, BO decreases $2 \to 1.5$. Stability decreases.

(4) $B_2/B_2^+$: Electron removed from bonding $\pi 2p$, BO decreases $1 \to 0.5$. Stability decreases.

The correct pair is $O_2/O_2^+$.

19966.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
19966.text: Among the following, which is not according to the property indicated against it?
options: $\mathrm{I}< \mathrm{Br}< \mathrm{F}< \mathrm{Cl} \text{ [Increasing Elecrtron Gain Enthalpy$ with negative sign] }
19966.sol:
Option (1): The electron gain enthalpy (magnitude) for halogens follows the order $\mathrm{I} < \mathrm{Br} < \mathrm{F} < \mathrm{Cl}$. Due to the small size of fluorine, interelectronic repulsions are high, making $\mathrm{Cl}$ have a more negative electron gain enthalpy than $\mathrm{F}$. This is correct.

Option (2): The first ionization enthalpy generally increases across a period. However, $\mathrm{N}$ has a stable half-filled $2p^3$ configuration, making its ionization enthalpy higher than that of $\mathrm{O}$. The correct order is $\mathrm{B} < \mathrm{C} < \mathrm{O} < \mathrm{N}$. Thus, the given statement is incorrect.

Option (3): For isoelectronic species, the ionic size increases as the nuclear charge decreases. The nuclear charges are $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+} (12)$, $\mathrm{Na}^{+} (11)$, $\mathrm{F}^{-} (9)$, and $\mathrm{O}^{2-} (8)$. The order $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+} < \mathrm{Na}^{+} < \mathrm{F}^{-} < \mathrm{O}^{2-}$ is correct.

Option (4): Metallic radii increase down a group due to the addition of new shells. The order $\mathrm{Na} < \mathrm{K} < \mathrm{Rb} < \mathrm{Cs}$ is correct.

Answer: $\mathrm{B}< \mathrm{C}< \mathrm{N}< \mathrm{O} \text{ [Increasing First Ionisation Enthalpy] }$

20063.subject: Chemistry
20063.text:
Two statements, one Assertion and the other Reason, are given. Choose the right option.
Assertion: The Standard Electrode potential, $\mathrm{E}^0 \mathrm{Co}^{3+} / \mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ is greater than $\mathrm{E}^0 \mathrm{Fe}^{3+} / \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$.
Reason: $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ ions are less stable in aqueous medium than $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ions which has stable $\mathrm{d}^5$ configuration
options: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
20063.sol:
The standard electrode potential $E^{0}$ for the reduction $M^{3+} + e^{-} \rightarrow M^{2+}$ depends on the stability of the $M^{3+}$ and $M^{2+}$ oxidation states in aqueous solution. For iron, the $Fe^{3+}$ ion has a stable $d^{5}$ configuration, making it relatively stable compared to $Fe^{2+}$ (d^{6}$), resulting in a lower reduction potential of $+0.77$ V.

For cobalt, the $Co^{3+}$ ion has a $d^{6}$ configuration and is a strong oxidizing agent because it is highly unstable in aqueous medium compared to $Co^{2+}$ (d^{7}$), which is more stable. Consequently, the reduction potential $E^{0} Co^{3+} / Co^{2+}$ is significantly higher, approximately $+1.97$ V.

Since the reduction potential of $Co^{3+} / Co^{2+}$ is greater than that of $Fe^{3+} / Fe^{2+}$, the Assertion is correct. The Reason correctly identifies that $Co^{3+}$ is less stable in aqueous medium than $Fe^{3+}$ (which has a stable $d^{5}$ configuration), and this difference in stability is the fundamental cause for the difference in their reduction potentials. Thus, the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

21513.subject: Mathematics
21513.text: If $x=2 a \sin ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{y}{2 a}}\right)-\sqrt{2 a y-y^2}$ then $\dfrac{d y}{d x}=$
21513.sol:
Given $x = 2a \sin^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{y}{2a}}\right) - \sqrt{2ay - y^2}$.

Let $y = 2a \sin^2 \theta$. Then \sqrt{$\dfrac{y}{2a}$} = $\sin \theta$$, so \theta = \sin^{-1} \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{y}{2a}}\right).

Also, \sqrt{2ay - y^2} = \sqrt{2a(2a \sin^2 \theta) - (2a \sin^2 \theta)^2} = \sqrt{4a^2 \sin^2 \theta (1 - \sin^2 \theta)} = \sqrt{4a^2 \sin^2 \theta \cos^2 \theta} =$2a \sin $\theta \cos \theta =$ a \sin(2$\theta).

Substituting these into the expression for $x$:

$x = 2a $\theta -$ a \sin(2$\theta).

Differentiating $x$ with respect to \theta:

\dfrac{dx}{d\theta} =$2a - 2a \cos(2$\theta) =$2a(1 - \cos(2$\theta)) =$2a(2 \sin^2 $\theta) =$4a \sin^2 $\theta.

Differentiating $y = 2a \sin^2 $\theta with respect to \theta:

\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} =$2a(2 \sin $\theta \cos \theta) =$4a \sin $\theta \cos \theta.

Using the chain rule \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}:

\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{4a \sin \theta \cos \theta}{4a \sin^2 \theta} = \dfrac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} = \cot \theta.

Since \sin^2 \theta = \dfrac{y}{2a}, we have \cos^2 \theta =$1 - $\dfrac{y}{2a} = \dfrac{2a - y}{2a}$.

Therefore, $\cot^2 \theta = \dfrac{\cos^2 \theta}{\sin^2 \theta} = \dfrac{(2a - y)/(2a)}{y/(2a)} = \dfrac{2a - y}{y}.$

Thus, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2a - y}{y}}.$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{2 a-y}{y}}$

21839.subject: Mathematics
21839.text: The number of four digit numbers strictly greater than 4321 formed using the digits $0,1,2,3,4,5$ with repetition of digit is
21839.sol:
The total number of four-digit numbers that can be formed using the digits $0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ with repetition is $5 \times 6 \times 6 \times 6 = 1080$.

We count the numbers less than or equal to $4321$.

Case 1: Numbers starting with $0$ are not four-digit numbers. So, the first digit can be $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$.

Case 2: Numbers starting with $1, 2, 3$:
First digit can be $1, 2, 3$ (3$ choices). The remaining three positions can be filled in 6 \times 6 \times 6 = 216$ ways. Total = $3 \times 216 = 648$.

Case 3: Numbers starting with $4$:
Subcase 3.1: Numbers starting with $40, 41, 42$:
First two digits are $40, 41, 42$ (3$ choices). The remaining two positions can be filled in 6 \times 6 = 36$ ways. Total = $3 \times 36 = 108$.

Subcase 3.2: Numbers starting with $430$:
First three digits are $430$. The last digit can be $0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ (6$ choices). Total = 6$.

Subcase 3.3: Numbers starting with $431$:
First three digits are $431$. The last digit can be $0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ (6$ choices). Total = 6$.

Subcase 3.4: Numbers starting with $4320, 4321$:
There are $2$ such numbers.

Total numbers $\le 4321$ is $648 + 108 + 6 + 6 + 2 = 770$.

The number of four-digit numbers strictly greater than $4321$ is $1080 - 770 = 310$.

Answer: 310

22171.text: The length of the perpendicular from the point $P(1,-1,2)$ to the given line $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{-3}=\dfrac{z+2}{4}$ is
22171.sol:
Let the line be $L: \dfrac{x+1}{2} = \dfrac{y-2}{-3} = \dfrac{z+2}{4} = \lambda$.

Any point $Q$ on the line $L$ is given by $Q(2\lambda - 1, -3\lambda + 2, 4\lambda - 2)$.

The vector $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ is given by $(2\lambda - 1 - 1, -3\lambda + 2 - (-1), 4\lambda - 2 - 2) = (2\lambda - 2, -3\lambda + 3, 4\lambda - 4)$.

Since $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ is perpendicular to the direction vector of the line $\vec{v} = (2, -3, 4)$, their dot product must be zero:

$(2\lambda - 2)(2) + (-3\lambda + 3)(-3) + (4\lambda - 4)(4) = 0$

$4\lambda - 4 + 9\lambda - 9 + 16\lambda - 16 = 0$

$29\lambda - 29 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 1$.

Substituting $\lambda = 1$ into the coordinates of $Q$, we get $Q(2(1) - 1, -3(1) + 2, 4(1) - 2) = Q(1, -1, 2)$.

Since the point $P(1, -1, 2)$ lies on the line, the length of the perpendicular from $P$ to the line is 0.

Answer: 0 units

22910.subject: Physics
22910.text: The acceleration due to gravity at pole and equator can be related as
22910.sol:
The acceleration due to gravity $g$ at a point on the surface of the Earth at a latitude $\lambda$ is given by the formula $g_{\lambda} = g - R\omega^2 \cos^2 \lambda$, where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity at the poles, $R$ is the radius of the Earth, and $\omega$ is the angular velocity of the Earth.

At the poles, the latitude $\lambda = 90^{{}^{\circ}}$. Substituting this into the formula, we get $g_p = g - R\omega^2 \cos^2(90^{{}^{\circ}}) = g - 0 = g$.

At the equator, the latitude $\lambda = 0^{{}^{\circ}}$. Substituting this into the formula, we get $g_e = g - R\omega^2 \cos^2(0^{{}^{\circ}}) = g - R\omega^2$.

Since $R\omega^2 > 0$, it follows that $g - R\omega^2 < g$. Therefore, $g_e < g_p$.

Answer: $g_e < g_p$

23473.subject: Physics
23473.text: In intrinsic semiconductors at room temperature, number of electrons and holes are
23473.sol:
In an intrinsic semiconductor, the charge carriers are generated solely due to thermal excitation of electrons from the valence band to the conduction band.

When an electron is excited to the conduction band, it leaves behind a vacancy in the valence band, which is referred to as a hole.

Since each thermal excitation produces exactly one electron in the conduction band and one hole in the valence band, the number density of electrons $n_e$ is equal to the number density of holes $n_h$.

Therefore, $n_e = n_h = n_i$, where $n_i$ is the intrinsic carrier concentration.

Answer: equal

23518.subject: Physics
23518.text: Two bodies of specific heats $C_1$ and $C_2$, having the same heat capacities are combined to form a single composite body. The specific heat capacity of the composite body is
23518.sol:
Let the masses of the two bodies be $m_1$ and $m_2$.

Given that their heat capacities are equal, we have $m_1 C_1 = m_2 C_2 = H$.

The masses can be written as $m_1 = \dfrac{H}{C_1}$ and $m_2 = \dfrac{H}{C_2}$.

For the composite body, the total heat capacity is $H_{total} = H + H = 2H$.

The total mass of the composite body is $M = m_1 + m_2 = \dfrac{H}{C_1} + \dfrac{H}{C_2}$.

The specific heat capacity of the composite body is $C = \dfrac{H_{total}}{M}$.

$C = \dfrac{2H}{\dfrac{H}{C_1} + \dfrac{H}{C_2}} = \dfrac{2}{\dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2}} = \dfrac{2C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}$

33605.text: Let $y = x + 2, 4y = 3x + 6$ and $3y = 4x + 1$ be three tangent lines to the circle $( x - h{)}^{2} + ( y - k{)}^{2} = {r}^{2}$. Then $h + k$ is equal to :
33605.sol:
Lines $y = x + 2$, $4y = 3x + 6$ and $3y = 4x + 1$ are tangents to the circle $( x - h{)}^{2} + ( y - k{)}^{2} = {r}^{2}$.

Centre of the circle is $\left(h, k\right)$.

Equation of bisector of lines $4y = 3x + 6, 3y = 4x + 1$ is:

$\dfrac{4x - 3y + 1}{5} = \pm \left(\dfrac{3x - 4y + 6}{5}\right)$

$⇒ 4x - 3y + 1 = \pm \left(3x - 4y + 6\right)$

Taking positive sign, we get

$4x - 3y + 1 = 3x - 4y + 6$

$⇒ x + y = 5$

Since, centre $\left(h, k\right)$ lies on the bisector, therefore

$h + k = 5$

34439.subject: Mathematics
34439.text:
Let $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$ be such that the system of linear equations
$x + 2y + z = 5$
$2x + y + \alpha z = 5$
$8x + 4y + \beta z = 18$
has no solution. Then $\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}$ is equal to :
34439.sol:
The given system of linear equations is:
$x + 2y + z = 5$
$2x + y + \alpha z = 5$
$8x + 4y + \beta z = 18$

For the system to have no solution, the determinant of the coefficient matrix $D$ must be zero.

$D = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & \alpha \\ 8 & 4 & \beta \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding along the first row:

$1(\beta - 4\alpha) - 2(2\beta - 8\alpha) + 1(8 - 8) = 0$

$\beta - 4\alpha - 4\beta + 16\alpha = 0$

$12\alpha - 3\beta = 0$

$\beta = 4\alpha$

To verify the no solution condition, substitute $\beta = 4\alpha$ into the third equation:

$8x + 4y + 4\alpha z = 18$

$4(2x + y + \alpha z) = 18$

$2x + y + \alpha z = \dfrac{9}{2}$

However, the second equation is $2x + y + \alpha z = 5$. This results in a contradiction since $\dfrac{9}{2} \neq 5$. Thus, the system has no solution when $\beta = 4\alpha$.

Therefore, $\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha} = 4$.

Answer: $4$

35713.sol:
Given that

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{e}^{ax} - cos ( bx ) - \dfrac{cx}{2}{e}^{- cx}}{1 - cos2x} = 17$

We know that ${e}^{ax} = 1 + ax + \dfrac{( ax{)}^{2}}{2 !} + \ldots$ and $cos\left(bx\right) = 1 - \dfrac{( bx{)}^{2}}{2 !} + \ldots$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 + ax + \dfrac{{\left(ax\right)}^{2}}{2 !} + \ldots\right) - \left(1 - \dfrac{{\left(bx\right)}^{2}}{2 !} + \ldots\right) - \dfrac{cx}{2}\left(1 - \left(cx\right) + \dfrac{{\left(cx\right)}^{2}}{2 !} - \ldots\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1 - cos2x}{{\left(2x\right)}^{2}}\right) \times 4{x}^{2}} = 17$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(a - \dfrac{c}{2}\right)x + \left(\dfrac{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}}{2}\right){x}^{2} + \ldots}{\dfrac{1}{2} \times 4{x}^{2}} = 17$

Now for limit to exist, $a - \dfrac{c}{2} = 0$$⇒ c = 2a$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}}{2}\right){x}^{2} + \ldots}{\dfrac{1}{2} \times 4{x}^{2}} = 17$

$⇒ \dfrac{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}}{4} = 17$

$⇒ {a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + 4{a}^{2} = 68$

$⇒ 5{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} = 68$

Hence this is the correct option.

$⇒ n = 3$  and ${2}^{m - n} = 8$

Distance between $P\left(6, 3\right)$ and $Q\left(- 2, - 3\right)$ is given by,

$PQ = \sqrt{{\left(6 + 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(3 + 3\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ PQ = \sqrt{{8}^{2} + {6}^{2}}$

$⇒ PQ = \sqrt{100}$

$⇒ PQ = 10$ units

38989.text: The ratio of wavelength of spectral lines ${H}_{\alpha}$ and ${H}_{\beta}$ in the Balmer series is $\dfrac{x}{20}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
38989.sol:
The formula to calculate the wavelength of ${H}_{\alpha}$-line in Balmer series is given by

$\dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}_{\alpha}} = 13 . 6\left[\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{9}\right] . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the wavelength of ${H}_{\beta}$-line in Balmer series is given by

$\dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}_{\beta}} = 13 . 6\left[\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{16}\right] . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1)
$⇒ \dfrac{{\lambda}_{\alpha}}{{\lambda}_{\beta}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{16}}{\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{9}}$
$= \dfrac{36}{64} \times \dfrac{12}{5}$
$= \dfrac{27}{20}$

39516.subject: Physics
39516.text: Two resistors of $200 \, \Omega$ and $400 \, \Omega$ are connected in series with a battery of $100$ V. A bulb rated at $200$ V, $100$ W is connected across the $400 \, \Omega$ resistance. The potential drop across the bulb is _______ V.
39516.sol:
The resistance of the bulb is calculated using its power rating:

$R_b = \dfrac{V^2}{P} = \dfrac{200^2}{100} = 400 \, \Omega$

The bulb is connected in parallel with the $400 \, \Omega$ resistor. The equivalent resistance of this parallel combination is:

$R_p = \dfrac{400 \times 400}{400 + 400} = 200 \, \Omega$

This parallel combination is in series with the $200 \, \Omega$ resistor. The total equivalent resistance of the circuit is:

$R_{eq} = 200 + R_p = 200 + 200 = 400 \, \Omega$

The current drawn from the battery is:

$I = \dfrac{V}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{100}{400} = 0.25 \text{ A}$

The potential drop across the bulb is the same as the potential drop across the parallel combination:

$V_p = I \times R_p = 0.25 \times 200 = 50 \text{ V}$

Answer: $50$

41792.text: Two resistance are given as ${R}_{1} = ( 10 \pm 0 . 5 ) Ω$ and ${R}_{2} = ( 15 \pm 0 . 5 ) Ω .$ The percentage error in the measurement of equivalent resistance when they are connected in parallel is
41792.sol:
For a parallel combination the equivalent resistance is

$\dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{{R}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{R}_{2}} . . . ( i )$

A general expression for error can be written as $x \pm ∆ x$

Differentiating equation (i)

$\dfrac{dR}{{R}^{2}} = d{R}_{1}{R}_{1}^{2} + d{R}_{2}{R}_{2}^{2} . . . ( ii )$

The equivalent resistance with ${R}_{1} = 10Ω \text{ and } {R}_{2} = 15Ω$ is

$\dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{15}$

$⇒ R = \dfrac{150}{25} = 6Ω$

Substituting the above value in equation (ii)

$dR = 36\left(\dfrac{0 . 5}{100} + \dfrac{0 . 5}{15 \times 15}\right) = 0 . 26$

$⇒ R = 6 \pm 0 . 26$

Hence, the percentage error is

$\dfrac{dR}{R} \times 100 = \dfrac{0 . 26}{6} \times 100$$= 4 . 33 %$

42491.text: The energy released if hydrogen atoms are combined to form $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ is __________ MeV. (Take binding energies per nucleon of $^{2}_{1}\text{H}$ and $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ as $1.1$ MeV and $7.2$ MeV, respectively)
42491.sol:
The fusion reaction is given by:

$2 ^{2}_{1}\text{H} \rightarrow ^{4}_{2}\text{He}$

Binding energy of one $^{2}_{1}\text{H}$ nucleus = $2 \times 1.1 = 2.2$ MeV

Total initial binding energy = $2 \times 2.2 = 4.4$ MeV

Binding energy of $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ nucleus = $4 \times 7.2 = 28.8$ MeV

Energy released $\Delta E$ = Final binding energy - Initial binding energy

$\Delta E = 28.8 - 4.4 = 24.4$ MeV

Answer: $24.4$

53815.text: To the lines $a x^2+2 h x y+b y^2=0$ the lines $a^2 x^2+2 h(a+b) x y+b^2 y^2=0$, are
53815.sol:
If the two pairs of straight lines have the same bisectors, then the two pairs are equally inclined.
The equation of the bisectors of the angle between the lines given by $a x^2+2 h x y+b y^2=0$ is
$\frac{x^2-y^2}{a-b}=\frac{x y}{h}...(i)$
The equation of the bisectors of the angle between the lines given by $a^2 x^2+2 h(a+b) x y+b^2 y^2=0 \text{ is }\frac{x^2-y^2}{a^2-b^2}=\frac{x y}{h(a+b)}\Rightarrow \frac{x^2-y^2}{a-b}=\frac{x y}{h}...(ii)$
Clearly Eqs. (i) and (ii) are the same. The two pairs of straight lines are equally inclined.

54857.text: Identify the name of reaction when phenol reacts with chloroform in aqueous NaOH.
54857.sol:
When phenol is treated with chloroform (CHCl_3$) in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide (NaOH$), an aldehyde group ($-CHO$) is introduced at the ortho position of the benzene ring. This reaction results in the formation of salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) as the major product.

This electrophilic substitution reaction, which proceeds via a dichlorocarbene ($:CCl_2$) intermediate, is known as the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.

Answer: Reimer-Tiemann reaction

A dihydric alcohol contains two hydroxyl (-OH) groups on a benzene ring in the context of phenols.

Catechol is benzene-1,2-diol, resorcinol is benzene-1,3-diol, and hydroquinone is benzene-1,4-diol—each has two hydroxyl groups.

Phloroglucinol is benzene-1,3,5-triol with three hydroxyl groups, making it trihydric rather than dihydric.

55464.text: Identify the carbon atom numbered from $\mathrm{C}_1{ }^{\prime}$ to $\mathrm{C}_5{ }^{\prime}$ of monosaccharide unit of DNA nucleotide that lacks oxygen atom from -OH group.
55464.sol:
The monosaccharide unit in DNA is deoxyribose, a pentose sugar distinguished from ribose by the absence of oxygen at the C-2′ position.
Ribose contains a hydroxyl group (-OH) at C-2′, whereas deoxyribose substitutes this with a hydrogen atom (-H).
All other carbon atoms (C-1′, C-3′, C-4′, C-5′) either include oxygen in hydroxyl groups, the furanose ring, or participate in glycosidic or phosphodiester bonds.

$\boxed{B}$

55465.subject: Chemistry
55465.text: Identify acidic amino acid from following list represented by three letter symbols.
55465.sol:
Amino acids are classified based on their side chain properties as neutral (polar or non-polar), acidic, or basic. Among the given options:

Threonine has a polar hydroxyl group, making it neutral polar. Tryptophan's indole ring classifies it as neutral non-polar. Histidine contains an imidazole group that can accept protons, classifying it as basic.

Glutamic acid possesses an additional carboxyl group in its side chain that donates protons, making it acidic.

55776.subject: Chemistry
55776.text: Identify the bond order of $\mathrm{NO}^{+}$ ion.
55776.sol:
The $\mathrm{NO}^{+}$ ion contains 14 electrons, with 7 from nitrogen and 8 from oxygen minus 1 due to the positive charge.

Its molecular orbital configuration follows the standard filling order for diatomic molecules: $(\sigma 1s)^2 (\sigma^* 1s)^2 (\sigma 2s)^2 (\sigma^* 2s)^2 (\pi 2p)^4 (\sigma 2p)^2$.

The bond order is calculated as half the difference between bonding and antibonding electrons. There are 10 bonding electrons ($\sigma 1s$, $\sigma 2s$, $\pi 2p$, and $\sigma 2p$) and 4 antibonding electrons ($\sigma^* 1s$ and $\sigma^* 2s$), giving $\frac{1}{2}(10 - 4) = 3$.

The bond order is $3$, corresponding to choice $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

56014.subject: Chemistry
56014.text: The rate constant for a first order reaction is $60 \text{ s}^{-1}$. How much time will it take to reduce the concentration of the reactant to $1/20^{\text{th}}$ of its initial value?
56014.sol:
For a first order reaction, the time required is given by the integrated rate equation:

$t = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{[R]_0}{[R]} \right)

Given $ k = 60 $\text{ s}^{-1} and the final concentration $[R] = $\dfrac{[R]_0}{20}.

Substituting the values into the equation:

$ t = $\dfrac{2.303}{60} \log \left( \dfrac{[R]_0}{\dfrac{[R]_0}{20}} \right)

$ t = $\dfrac{2.303}{60} \log(20)$

Using $\log(20) = \log(2 \times10) = \log 2 + \log 10 = 0.3010 + 1 = 1.3010$:

$t = \dfrac{2.303 \times 1.3010}{60}

$ t = $\dfrac{2.9962}{60}

$ t $\approx0.0499 \text{ s}

Answer: 0.0499$ s

56440.subject: Chemistry
56440.text: $Find the total number of moles of donor atoms present in one mole \mathrm{K}_{4} \left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right] complex.$
56440.sol:
The complex $\mathrm{K}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ contains the coordination ion $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{4-}$ with iron as the central metal atom coordinated by six cyanide ligands.

Cyanide is monodentate with carbon serving as the donor atom, contributing one donor site per ligand.

Since there are six ligands, each providing one donor atom, one mole of the complex contains exactly six moles of donor atoms.

$\boxed{6}$

56466.subject: Chemistry
56466.text: Identify pair of complexes that exhibits solvate isomerism.
56466.sol:
Solvate isomerism occurs when solvent molecules are both coordinated ligands and present as lattice entities, with identical overall formulas but differing coordination environments.

Consider option A:
$\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3$ has all six water molecules coordinated, while $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_5 \mathrm{Cl}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ has five coordinated waters and one lattice water, both corresponding to $\mathrm{CrCl}_3 \cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$.

Option B exhibits ionization isomerism, C exhibits coordination isomerism, and D exhibits linkage isomerism.

The pair demonstrating solvate isomerism is $\boxed{A}$.

58833.subject: Chemistry
58833.text: In a fcc arrangement of A and B atoms in which 'A' atoms are at the corners of the unit cell and 'B' atoms are at the face centers. One of the 'A' atoms is missing from one corner in unit cell. What is the simplest formula of a compound ?
58833.sol:
In an fcc unit cell, there are $8$ corners and $6$ face centers.

Since one 'A' atom is missing from a corner, the number of 'A' atoms at the corners is $7$.

Contribution of each corner atom to the unit cell is $\dfrac{1}{8}$.

Effective number of 'A' atoms per unit cell = $7 \times \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{7}{8}$

The 'B' atoms are at the $6$ face centers.

Contribution of each face center atom to the unit cell is $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Effective number of 'B' atoms per unit cell = $6 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 3$

Ratio of atoms A to B = $\dfrac{7}{8} : 3 = 7 : 24$

The simplest formula of the compound is $\text{A}_7\text{B}_{24}$.

Answer: $\text{A}_7\text{B}_{24}$

58844.subject: Chemistry
58844.text: Calculate the radius of an atom of an element in pm if it forms bcc unit cell structure having edge length $4.3 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{ cm}$.
58844.sol:
Body-centered cubic structure atoms contact along the body diagonal, whose length equals $4r$.

The body diagonal relates to edge length $a$ through spatial geometry: $a\sqrt{3} = 4r$.

Isolating the radius yields $r = \frac{a\sqrt{3}}{4}$.

Given edge length $a = 4.3 \times 10^{-8}$ cm converts to $a = 430$ pm using $1$ cm $= 10^{10}$ pm.

Substitution gives $r = \frac{430 \times \sqrt{3}}{4}$.

With $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.732$, the calculation proceeds: $r = \frac{430 \times 1.732}{4} = \frac{744.76}{4} = 186.19$ pm.

The approximate radius of $186.2$ pm corresponds to option A.

60192.subject: Mathematics
60192.text: A tank with a rectangular base and rectangular sides, open at the top is made. Depth of the tank is $4$ m and its volume is $36$ cubic meters. For making a tank cost of base material used is Rs. $100$ per sq. meter and that of sides is Rs. $50$ per sq. meter. Then minimum cost of tank is..............
60192.sol:
Let the length and breadth of the base of the tank be $x$ and $y$ respectively.

Given depth $h = 4$ m and volume $V = 36$ m$^3$.

$V = x \times y \times h \Rightarrow 4xy = 36 \Rightarrow xy = 9$

Cost of the base $= 100 \times xy = 100 \times 9 = 900$

Area of the four sides $= 2(xh + yh) = 2(4)(x + y) = 8(x + y)$

Cost of the sides $= 50 \times 8(x + y) = 400(x + y)$

Total cost $C = 900 + 400(x + y)$

To minimize $C$, we need to minimize $x + y$.

Using AM-GM inequality for $x, y \gt 0$:

$\dfrac{x + y}{2} \geq \sqrt{xy}$

$x + y \geq 2\sqrt{9} = 6$

Minimum value of $x + y$ is $6$, which occurs when $x = y = 3$.

Minimum cost $C = 900 + 400(6) = 900 + 2400 = 3300$

Answer: Rs. $3300$

60290.subject: Mathematics
60290.text: By dropping a stone in a quiet lake, a wave in the form of circle is generated. The radius of the circular wave increases at the rate of $2.1 \mathrm{ cm} / \mathrm\sec$. Then the rate of increase of the enclosed circular region, when the radius of the circular wave is 10 cm, is (Given $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
60290.sol:
Differentiating the area formula $A = \pi r^2$ with respect to time using the chain rule gives the relation $\frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r \frac{dr}{dt}$.

Substituting the given values $r = 10\text{ cm}$, $\frac{dr}{dt} = 2.1\text{ cm/s}$, and using $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ yields:
$\frac{dA}{dt} = 2 \cdot \frac{22}{7} \cdot 10 \cdot 2.1 = 2 \cdot \frac{22}{7} \cdot 10 \cdot \frac{21}{10}$.

Simplifying the expression by canceling the factor of 10 and evaluating $\frac{21}{7}$ gives:
$\frac{dA}{dt} = 2 \cdot 22 \cdot 3 = 132$.

The area increases at a rate of $132\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}$ when the radius is 10 cm.

$\boxed{C}$

60737.text: The number of integral values of $K$ for which $x^2+\mathrm{y}^2+\mathrm{k} x+(1-\mathrm{k}) \mathrm{y}+5=0$ represents a circle whose radius cannot exceeds 5, are
60737.sol:
The circle equation is $x^2 + y^2 + Kx + (1-K)y + 5 = 0$. Comparing with the standard form $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$, we identify $2g = K$, $2f = 1-K$, and $c = 5$.

The radius squared is $r^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c = \left(\frac{K}{2}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{1-K}{2}\right)^2 - 5 = \frac{2K^2 - 2K + 1}{4} - 5$.

Given $r \leq 5$, it follows that $r^2 \leq 25$.

$2K^2 - 2K - 119 \leq 0$

The roots of $2K^2 - 2K - 119 = 0$ are $K = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{956}}{4} \approx \frac{2 \pm 30.919}{4}$, yielding $K_1 \approx -7.22975$ and $K_2 \approx 8.22975$.

The inequality holds for $K$ between these roots: $-7.22975 \leq K \leq 8.22975$.

The integral values within this range are $K = -7, -6, \ldots, 8$, which total $8 - (-7) + 1 = 16$.

61975.subject: Mathematics
61975.text: The eccentricity of the ellipse $9 x^2+5 y^2-30 y=0$ is
61975.sol:
To determine the eccentricity of the ellipse defined by $9x^2 + 5y^2 - 30y = 0$, the equation is first transformed into standard form by completing the square.

Rewriting the equation: $9x^2 + 5(y^2 - 6y) = 0$.
Completing the square: $9x^2 + 5[(y - 3)^2 - 9] = 0$, which simplifies to $9x^2 + 5(y - 3)^2 = 45$.

Dividing through by 45 yields the standard form: $\frac{x^2}{5} + \frac{(y - 3)^2}{9} = 1$.

The larger denominator, $a^2 = 9$, corresponds to the semi-major axis, while $b^2 = 5$ is the semi-minor axis squared. The eccentricity is given by $e = \sqrt{1 - \frac{b^2}{a^2}} = \sqrt{1 - \frac{5}{9}} = \frac{2}{3}$.

Among the options, $\frac{2}{3}$ corresponds to choice B.

Let mean and standard deviation of probability distribution $

P(X= x)\frac{1}{4}K\frac{1}{4}\frac{1}{3}
$\) be $\mu$ and $\sigma$ respectively and if $\sigma-\mu=2$ then $\sigma=$
63632.sol:
The sum of probabilities must equal 1, so K is found from

$\frac{1}{4} + K + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{3} = 1$

yielding $K = \frac{1}{6}$.

The mean is $\mu = \sum xP(X=x) = (-3)\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + 0\left(\frac{1}{6}\right) + 1\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + \alpha\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\alpha}{3}$.

The second moment is $E(X^2) = 9\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + 0 + 1\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + \alpha^2\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{5}{2} + \frac{\alpha^2}{3}$.

The variance becomes $\sigma^2 = E(X^2) - \mu^2 = \frac{5}{2} + \frac{\alpha^2}{3} - \left(-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\alpha}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4} + \frac{2\alpha^2}{9} + \frac{\alpha}{3}$.

Given $\sigma - \mu = 2$, squaring gives $\sigma^2 = (\mu + 2)^2 = \left(\frac{3}{2} + \frac{\alpha}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4} + \alpha + \frac{\alpha^2}{9}$.

Equating both expressions for $\sigma^2$ and simplifying leads to $\alpha^2 - 6\alpha = 0$, so $\alpha(\alpha - 6) = 0$.

The solution $\alpha = 0$ is invalid as it creates conflicting probabilities for $x=0$, leaving $\alpha = 6$.

With $\alpha = 6$, $\mu = -\frac{1}{2} + \frac{6}{3} = \frac{3}{2}$, and $\sigma = \mu + 2 = \frac{7}{2}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\frac{7}{2}}$

63714.text: Two cards are drawn' successively with replacement from a well shuffled pack of 52 cards. Then mean of number of kings is
63714.sol:
Let X denote the number of king.
Since the card is drawn twice, 0,1 and 2 are possible values of X.
Probability of getting a king in a single draw of $a$ card is $p=\frac{4}{52}=\frac{1}{13}, q=\frac{12}{13}\begin{aligned}
& P[X=0]=P[\text{ no king }]=q q=q^2=\frac{144}{169} \\
& \mathrm{P}[\mathrm{X}=1]=\mathrm{P}[\text{ one king }]=\mathrm{pq}+\mathrm{qp}=2 \mathrm{pq}=\frac{24}{169} \\
& \mathrm{P}[\mathrm{X}=2]=\mathrm{P}[\text{ two kings }]=\mathrm{pp}=\mathrm{p}^2=\frac{1}{169} \\
& \text{ Mean }=\sum x_{\mathrm{i}} \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{i}} \\
& =0 \times \frac{144}{169}+1 \times \frac{24}{169}+2 \times \frac{1}{169} \\
& =\frac{26}{169}=\frac{2}{13}
\end{aligned}$
Alternate method:
Let getting a king be the success.
$p=\frac{1}{13}, q=\frac{12}{13}$Since two cards are drawn with replacement.
$\therefore \quad n=2$Here, r.v. $X \sim B\left(\frac{1}{13}, 2\right)\therefore \quad \text{ mean }=\mathrm{np}=\frac{2}{13}$

65162.text: if $\bar{a}, \overline{\mathrm{ b}}, \overline{\mathrm{c}}$ are non coplanar unit vectors such that $\bar{a} \times(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})=\frac{\overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}}}{\sqrt{2}}$ Then the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ is
65162.sol:
Given $\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = \frac{\bar{b} + \bar{c}}{\sqrt{2}}$, expand the triple product using the identity $\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c}$.

This yields $(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bar{b} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bar{c}$.

Since $\bar{a}$, $\bar{b}$, and $\bar{c}$ are non-coplanar unit vectors and thus linearly independent, equate coefficients:

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$-(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Solving gives $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

For unit vectors, the dot product equals $\cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$. Thus, $\cos \theta = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, so $\theta = \frac{3\pi}{4}$.

The angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ is $\frac{3\pi}{4}$.

$x^2 = n(A² - x²)$

$\dfrac{n}{n+1} =$$\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)$^$$2

$\dfrac{n}{n+1} = \dfrac{8}{9}$$

$9n = 8n + 8$

$n = 8$

$\alpha = \dfrac{\beta}{1 + \beta}$

Substituting the value of $\beta$:

We also know that $\alpha = \dfrac{I_C}{I_E}$, where $I_C$ is the collector current.

Substituting the values:

$I_C = \dfrac{20}{21} \times 7 = \dfrac{20}{3}$ mA

69446.text: When LED is manufactured by using aluminium gallium arsenide (AlGaAs), it emits
69446.sol:
The emitted color of an LED corresponds to the band gap energy of its semiconductor material. AlGaAs has a band gap that typically produces infrared radiation when electrons and holes recombine at the p-n junction.

Variations in aluminium composition allow tuning of the band gap, but AlGaAs LEDs predominantly emit in the infrared spectrum, as seen in devices like remote controls and optical communication systems. Other materials such as GaN or InGaN are required for ultraviolet, green, or blue emission.

Statement (I) is correct because ecological pyramids assume a simple food chain, which almost never exists in nature, and they do not accommodate a food web.

Therefore, Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

71211.subject: Biology
71211.text: Which one of the following is INCORRECT about organic fertilizers and biofertilizers?
options: Former is formed from product or dead material of biological origin.
Organic fertilizers increase fertility of soil while later helps in nitrogen fixation
Biofertilizers include use of live bacterial or fungal organisms to enrich the nutrient quality of soil.
It includes addition of inorganic minerals in definite proportion in the field.
71211.sol:
Organic fertilizers are derived from animal matter, animal excreta, human excreta, and vegetable matter (e.g., compost and crop residues). They are formed from products or dead materials of biological origin.

Biofertilizers are preparations containing living cells or latent cells of efficient strains of microorganisms (bacteria, fungi, algae) that help crop plants' uptake of nutrients by their interactions in the rhizosphere, such as nitrogen fixation and phosphorus solubilization.

Inorganic or chemical fertilizers involve the addition of inorganic minerals in definite proportions to the field. Therefore, the statement that organic and biofertilizers include the addition of inorganic minerals in definite proportions is incorrect.

Answer: It includes addition of inorganic minerals in definite proportion in the field.

72060.subject: Chemistry
72060.text: Determine the temperature at which $2$ moles of oxygen gas expands isothermally and reversibly from $2\ \text{dm}^3$ to $20\ \text{dm}^3$ performs $-11490\ \text{J}$ of work $[2.303 \times R = 19.15\ \text{JK}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}]$
72060.sol:
The work done during a reversible isothermal expansion is given by:

$W = -2.303 nRT \log_{10} \left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right)

Substituting the given values $ W = -11490\ $\text{J}, $ n = 2\ $\text{mol}, $ V_1 = 2\ $\text{dm}^3$, $V_2 = 20\ \text{dm}^3$, and $2.303 R = 19.15\ \text{J K}^{-1} \text{mol}^{-1}:

$-11490 = -2 $\times19.15 \times$ T $\times \log_{10} \left(\dfrac{20}{2}\right)

$-11490 = -38.3 $\times$ T $\times \log_{10}(10)$

$-11490 = -38.3 \times$ T $\times1$

$T = \dfrac{11490}{38.3} =300\ \text{K}

Answer: 300\ \text{K}$

83002.subject: Physics
83002.text: A bar magnet of length $l$ and magnetic dipole moment $M$ is bent in the form of an arc as shown in figure. The new magnetic dipole moment will be
83002.sol:
Given, \(\theta=60^{\circ}=\frac{\pi}{3} \mathrm{rad}\)
The new magnetic length of the dipole will be, \(I^{\prime}=r\)
Now, \(M=m \cdot I\) and \(M^{\prime}=m \cdot I^{\prime}\)
\(\therefore \frac{\mathrm{M}}{\mathrm{M}^{\prime}}=\frac{\mathrm{I}}{\mathrm{I}^{\prime}} \ldots \quad (1)\)
Now, angle in radians \(=\frac{\text{ arc length }}{\text{ radius }}\)
\(\therefore \frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{1}{r} \Rightarrow 1=\frac{\pi r}{3}\)
In the equilateral triangle, marked by dotted lines, \(I^{\prime}=r\)
\(\therefore \frac{1}{I^{\prime}}=\frac{\pi}{3} \ldots \quad (2)\)
From and, we get,
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{M}{M^{\prime}}=\frac{\pi}{3} \\
& \therefore M^{\prime}=\frac{3 M}{\pi}\end{aligned}\)
Hence, \((C)\) is$ the $correct answer.
Alternative method:
Using the short cut formula about bending of a bar magnet, \(M=\frac{2 M \sin \left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)}{\theta}\)
\(=\frac{2 M \sin 30^{\circ}}{\frac{\pi}{3}}=\frac{3 M}{\pi}\)
Hence, (C) is the correct answer.$

84870.subject: Zoology
84870.text: Which of the following RNAs is not required for the synthesis of protein?
84870.sol:
The process of synthesis of protein is called translation. It utilizes three types of RNA for the process:

(1) mRNA: It carries the message for a sequence of amino acids in the form of genetic codons.
(2) tRNA: It carries amino acids at its $3 '$ end in charged form. Also, it has an anticodon loop to identify codons of mRNA.
(3) rRNA: It forms the ribosomal subunits and hence is called ribosomal RNA. Ribosomes are called protein factories of the cell.

siRNA or small interfering RNA is not used in the protein synthesis mechanism, it interferes with the synthesis of proteins.

85072.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Logistic growth I. Unlimited resource availability condition
B. Exponential growth II. Limited resource availability condition
C. Expanding age pyramid III. The percent individuals of pre-reproductive age is largest followed by reproductive and post reproductive age groups
D. Stable age pyramid IV. The percent individuals of pre-reproductives and reproductive age group are same

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
85072.sol:
• When there is limited resources available, in nature, there is sheer competition and only the fittest can survive. This indicates a logistic growth curve in the population.
  • If there are unlimited resources, the chances of competitions are rather less. This leads to exponential growth of the population.
  • In expanding age pyramid of a population, the percent individuals of pre-reproductive age is largest followed by reproductive and post reproductive age groups.
  • Conversely, in a stable population, the percent individuals of pre-reproductives and reproductive age group are nearly the same.

85086.subject: Zoology
85086.text:
Match the items in Column$- I$ with those in Column$- II$:

Column$- I$ Column$- II$
(a) Herbivores-Plants (i) Commensalism
(b) Mycorrhiza-Plants (ii) Mutualism
(c) Sheep-Cattle (iii) Predation
(d) Orchid-Tree (iv) Competition

Select the correct option from following:
85086.sol:
Mycorrhiza: This is a mutualistic relationship between fungi and roots of higher plants. Fungi absorb essential nutrients from the soil while the plants, in turn, provide energy-yielding carbohydrates to the fungi.

Competition in the broadest sense refers to the interaction of two organisms striving for the same resource. Sheep and cattle both are herbivores and fight for the same resource when present together. It is an example of an interspecific competition.

In predation, only one species (predator) benefits and the interaction is detrimental to the other species (prey). Herbivores are predators and plants are prey.

Epiphytes (orchids) growing on other plants like mango (host) gets benefit in the form of shelter but the host neither drives any apparent benefit nor does it get harmed. Such an interaction is called commensalism.

85701.subject: Biology
85701.text: Female beetles are known to prefer males with bigger mandibles. In an experiment, a population of these beetles were picked and divided into two groups. For one group, only those males who had larger than average mandible size were allowed to mate to produce next-generation offspring (group 1). For the other group, the males and females were allowed to mate randomly (group 2). These populations were maintained using this regime for 50 generations. After this, it was found that the male mandible size in group 1 was significantly larger than that of group 2. However, the females in group 1 produced fewer offspring than females in group 2. Possible explanation(s) of this observation is(are)
options: In the experiment, as selection on female reproduction was not imposed in group 1 , female reproductive capability declined over time.

Group 1 males produced offspring with larger thorax (to support larger mandible) and hence smaller abdomen, which influenced the egg-carrying capacity in female offspring leading to a decline in female reproductive ability.

Under unlimited food condition, males with larger mandibles in group 1 , preferred females with lesser reproductive ability as that allowed dominant individual males to have more resources for themselves.
Under limited food condition, females producing fitter offspring after mating with males with larger mandibles started producing fever offspring to nourish them better.

92689.text: Two blocks $A$ and $B$ of masses $m$ and $2m$ are connected by a massless spring of force constant $k$ and are placed on a smooth horizontal plane. The spring is stretched by an amount $x$ and then released. The relative velocity of the blocks when the spring comes to its natural length is
92689.sol:
Let us assume the velocity of block& $A$ and& $B$ are& ${v}_{1}$ and& ${v}_{2}$ respectively.

Relative velocity will be ${v}_{1} + {v}_{2}$

Using conservation of linear momentum

$m{v}_{1} = 2m{v}_{2}$

$⇒ {v}_{1} = 2{v}_{2}$

Using conservation of energy

$\dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}2m{v}_{2}^{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\left(2{v}_{2}\right)}^{2} + m{v}_{2}^{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2} = 2m{v}_{2}^{2} + m{v}_{2}^{2}$

$3m{v}_{2}^{2} = \dfrac{kx^{2}}{2}$

${v}_{2}^{2} = \dfrac{kx^{2}}{6m}$

${v}_{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{6m}} . x$

Relative velocity $= 3{v}_{2}$

$= 3\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{6m}} . x$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{3k}{2m}} . x$

95860.text: In some fungi such as _____, the fusion of two haploid cells immediately results in diploid cell while in other group of fungi like _____, an intervening dikaryotic stage occurs, called dikaryophase.
95860.sol:
In Fungi, sexual reproduction occurs by formation and fusion of two gametes with their nuclei. This type of reproduction is absent in the fungi group - Deuteromycetes.

In Sexual reproduction, the there is fusion of the nuclei as well as the cytoplasm. The former is referred to as Karyogamy and later as Plasmogamy. In fungi group, Basidiomycetes and Ascomycetes, the karyogamy is delayed and takes place just before meiosis. In the stage intervening between plasmogamy and karyogamy the cells often contain two nuclei or Dikaryons (n+n) and the phase is known as dikaryophase. The life cycle of the such fungi have three phases.

Fungi group like Phycomycetes, dikaryophase is absent and fusion of the haploid gametes forms diploid cells.

100118.subject: Physics
100118.text: The energy density $u$ of a system is given by the relation $u = \dfrac{\alpha}{\beta} \sin\left(\dfrac{\alpha x}{k_B T}\right)$, where $x$ is distance, $k_B$ is the Boltzmann constant, and $T$ is absolute temperature. The SI base unit of the constant $\beta$ is:
100118.sol:
The argument of the sine function must be dimensionless. Therefore,
$\left[\dfrac{\alpha x}{k_B T}\right] = [\mathrm{M}^0 \mathrm{L}^0 \mathrm{T}^0]$

The term $k_B T$ represents thermal energy, so its dimensional formula is $[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^2 \mathrm{T}^{-2}]$.
Substituting the dimensions of distance $x$ as $[\mathrm{L}]$:
$[\alpha] = \dfrac{[k_B T]}{[x]} = \dfrac{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^2 \mathrm{T}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{L}]} = [\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L} \mathrm{T}^{-2}]$

The quantity $u$ is energy density (energy per unit volume), so its dimensional formula is:
$[u] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^2 \mathrm{T}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{L}^3]} = [\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^{-1} \mathrm{T}^{-2}]$

From the given equation, the dimensions of $u$ must equal the dimensions of $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$:
$[\beta] = \dfrac{[\alpha]}{[u]} = \dfrac{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L} \mathrm{T}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^{-1} \mathrm{T}^{-2}]} = [\mathrm{L}^2]$

The SI base unit for $[\mathrm{L}^2]$ is $\mathrm{m}^2$.

Answer: $\mathrm{m}^2$

101378.subject: Physics
101378.text: A mass $m$ is moved from the bottom of a mine of depth $d = \dfrac{R}{2}$ to a height $h = \dfrac{R}{2}$ above the surface of the Earth. If $R$ is the radius of the Earth and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity at its surface, the total work done in this process is:
101378.sol:
The gravitational potential energy of a mass $m$ at a distance $r$ from the centre of the Earth (where $r < R$) is given by:
$U = -\dfrac{GMm}{2R^3}(3R^2 - r^2)$

At a depth $d = \dfrac{R}{2}$, the distance from the centre is $r = R - \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{R}{2}$.
Initial potential energy, $U_i = -\dfrac{GMm}{2R^3}\left(3R^2 - \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2\right) = -\dfrac{GMm}{2R^3}\left(3R^2 - \dfrac{R^2}{4}\right) = -\dfrac{11GMm}{8R}$

At a height $h = \dfrac{R}{2}$, the distance from the centre is $r = R + \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{3R}{2}$.
Final potential energy, $U_f = -\dfrac{GMm}{r} = -\dfrac{GMm}{\dfrac{3R}{2}} = -\dfrac{2GMm}{3R}$

The total work done is the change in potential energy:
$W = U_f - U_i = -\dfrac{2GMm}{3R} - \left(-\dfrac{11GMm}{8R}\right) = \left(\dfrac{11}{8} - \dfrac{2}{3}\right)\dfrac{GMm}{R}$
$W = \left(\dfrac{33 - 16}{24}\right)\dfrac{GMm}{R} = \dfrac{17}{24}\dfrac{GMm}{R}$

Since $g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}$, we have $\dfrac{GMm}{R} = mgR$.
Therefore, $W = \dfrac{17}{24} mgR$.

Answer: $\dfrac{17}{24} mgR$

102464.subject: Physics
102464.text: Two identical blocks are attached to two separate massless springs having spring constants $k_1$ and $k_2$. They are made to oscillate vertically such that the maximum acceleration of both blocks is exactly the same. The ratio of the amplitude of the first block to the amplitude of the second block ($A_1 / A_2$) is:
102464.sol:
Let the mass of each identical block be $m$.

The maximum acceleration of a block executing simple harmonic motion is given by $a_{\max} = A\omega^2$, where $A$ is the amplitude and $\omega$ is the angular frequency.

For a spring-mass system, $\omega^2 = \dfrac{k}{m}$.

Thus, the maximum acceleration is $a_{\max} = A\left(\dfrac{k}{m}\right)$.

Given that the maximum accelerations are equal for both blocks:
$A_1\left(\dfrac{k_1}{m}\right) = A_2\left(\dfrac{k_2}{m}\right)$

Since the masses are identical, $m$ cancels out:
$A_1 k_1 = A_2 k_2$

Rearranging this gives the ratio of their amplitudes:
$\dfrac{A_1}{A_2} = \dfrac{k_2}{k_1}$

Answer: $\dfrac{k_2}{k_1}$

Since the lower power bulb has a higher resistance, it will dissipate more power (\(P=I^2 R\)), meaning it will emit more light than the higher power rating bulb. So, Assertion (A) is true.
- Reason (R): In a series circuit, the current is the same for all components. Hence, it is incorrect to say that the lower power bulb gets more current than the higher power rating bulb. Thus, Reason (R) is false.

104104.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a series LCR circuit with $L = 0.1\text{ H}$ and $C = 10\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ connected to an AC source $V = 200 \sin(1000t)$, the power factor is unity.
Reason (R): The linear frequency ($\nu$) of the AC source is $1000\text{ Hz}$, which is equal to the resonant frequency ($\nu_0$) of the circuit.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
104104.sol:
For the given AC source $V = 200 \sin(1000t)$, the angular frequency is $\omega = 1000\text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

The resonant angular frequency of the circuit is:
$\omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{0.1 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}}} = 1000\text{ rad s}^{-1}$

Since $\omega = \omega_0$, the circuit is at resonance and the power factor is unity ($\cos\phi = 1$). Thus, Assertion (A) is true.

The linear frequency of the source is $\nu = \dfrac{\omega}{2\pi} = \dfrac{1000}{2\pi} = \dfrac{500}{\pi}\text{ Hz}$.
The value $1000$ refers to the angular frequency, not the linear frequency. Thus, Reason (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false.

104147.text:
An alternating voltage given by the equation $v(t) = 200 \sin(100t)$ is applied across a pure capacitor of capacitance $50 \mu\text{F}$. The corresponding time-domain equation for the current $i(t)$ in the circuit is:
(Assume $v(t)$ is in volts, $i(t)$ is in amperes, and $t$ is in seconds)
104147.sol:
Comparing the given voltage equation $v(t) = 200 \sin(100t)$ with the standard form $v(t) = V_0 \sin(\omega t)$, we get:
Peak voltage, $V_0 = 200$ V
Angular frequency, $\omega = 100$ rad/s

The capacitive reactance is:
$X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{100 \times 50 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{1}{5 \times 10^{-3}} = 200 \Omega$

The peak current is:
$I_0 = \dfrac{V_0}{X_C} = \dfrac{200}{200} = 1.0$ A

In a purely capacitive circuit, the current leads the voltage by a phase angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Therefore, the equation for the current is:
$i(t) = I_0 \sin(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}) = 1.0 \sin(100t + \dfrac{\pi}{2})$

Answer: $i(t) = 1.0 \sin(100t + \dfrac{\pi}{2})$

104492.subject: Physics
104492.text: A right-angled prism (refracting angle $A = 90^{\circ}$) is completely immersed in a transparent liquid of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$. A light ray hits one face of the prism at an angle of incidence of $45^{\circ}$ and emerges grazing the second face. The refractive index of the prism glass is:
104492.sol:
Let the refractive index of the prism be $\mu_g$ and that of the liquid be $\mu_L = \sqrt{2}$.

At the first face, applying Snell's law:
$\mu_L \sin i = \mu_g \sin r_1$

At the second face, the ray grazes the surface, so the angle of refraction is $90^{\circ}$ and the angle of incidence is the critical angle $c$ for the glass-liquid interface:
$\mu_g \sin c = \mu_L \sin 90^{\circ} \Rightarrow \sin c = \dfrac{\mu_L}{\mu_g}$

For a prism, $r_1 + c = A$. Given $A = 90^{\circ}$, we have $r_1 = 90^{\circ} - c$.
Therefore, $\sin r_1 = \sin(90^{\circ} - c) = \cos c = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 c} = \sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{\mu_L}{\mu_g}\right)^2}$.

Substituting this into the first Snell's law equation:
$\mu_L \sin i = \mu_g \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{\mu_L^2}{\mu_g^2}} = \sqrt{\mu_g^2 - \mu_L^2}$

Squaring both sides:
$\mu_L^2 \sin^2 i = \mu_g^2 - \mu_L^2$
$\mu_g^2 = \mu_L^2 (1 + \sin^2 i)$

Given $\mu_L = \sqrt{2}$ and $i = 45^{\circ}$:
$\mu_g^2 = (\sqrt{2})^2 \left(1 + \sin^2 45^{\circ}\right) = 2 \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 2 \times \dfrac{3}{2} = 3$

Thus, $\mu_g = \sqrt{3}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{3}$

104871.subject: Physics
104871.text: Consider an electron in the second stationary orbit of a $\text{He}^{+}$ ion and an electron in the first stationary orbit of a hydrogen atom. What is the ratio of the area enclosed by the orbit of the $\text{He}^{+}$ ion to the area enclosed by the orbit of the hydrogen atom?
104871.sol:
The radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit for a hydrogen-like species is given by:
$r \propto \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$

For the $\text{He}^{+}$ ion in the second orbit ($n=2, Z=2$):
$r_{\text{He}^{+}} \propto \dfrac{2^2}{2} = 2$

For the hydrogen atom in the first orbit ($n=1, Z=1$):
$r_{\text{H}} \propto \dfrac{1^2}{1} = 1$

The ratio of their radii is:
$\dfrac{r_{\text{He}^{+}}}{r_{\text{H}}} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

Assuming the orbits to be circular, the area enclosed by an orbit is $A = \pi r^2$.
Therefore, the ratio of the areas is proportional to the square of the ratio of their radii:
$\dfrac{A_{\text{He}^{+}}}{A_{\text{H}}} = \left( \dfrac{r_{\text{He}^{+}}}{r_{\text{H}}} \right)^2 = \left( \dfrac{2}{1} \right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{1}$

The required ratio is $4:1$.

Answer: $4:1$

105250.subject: Physics
105250.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Boolean Expression)List-II (Logic Gate)
(P) $Y = \overline{\overline{A} \cdot \overline{B}}$(1) AND
(Q) $Y = \overline{A} \cdot \overline{B}$(2) OR
(R) $Y = \overline{\overline{A} + \overline{B}}$(3) NAND
(S) $Y = \overline{A} + \overline{B}$(4) NOR

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
105250.sol:
Let us simplify each Boolean expression using De Morgan's laws:

(P) $Y = \overline{\overline{A} \cdot \overline{B}}$
Applying De Morgan's law ($\overline{X \cdot Y} = \overline{X} + \overline{Y}$):
$Y = \overline{\overline{A}} + \overline{\overline{B}} = A + B$
This is the expression for an OR gate. So, P matches with (2).

(Q) $Y = \overline{A} \cdot \overline{B}$
Applying De Morgan's law ($\overline{X} \cdot \overline{Y} = \overline{X + Y}$):
$Y = \overline{A + B}$
This is the expression for a NOR gate. So, Q matches with (4).

(R) $Y = \overline{\overline{A} + \overline{B}}$
Applying De Morgan's law ($\overline{X + Y} = \overline{X} \cdot \overline{Y}$):
$Y = \overline{\overline{A}} \cdot \overline{\overline{B}} = A \cdot B$
This is the expression for an AND gate. So, R matches with (1).

(S) $Y = \overline{A} + \overline{B}$
Applying De Morgan's law ($\overline{X} + \overline{Y} = \overline{X \cdot Y}$):
$Y = \overline{A \cdot B}$
This is the expression for a NAND gate. So, S matches with (3).

The correct matching sequence is P-(2), Q-(4), R-(1), S-(3).

Answer: P-(2), Q-(4), R-(1), S-(3)

105548.subject: Physics
105548.text: A proton and an alpha particle are accelerated from rest through potential differences $V_p$ and $V_\alpha$, respectively. If their associated de-Broglie wavelengths are found to be equal, what is the ratio of $V_p$ to $V_\alpha$?
105548.sol:
The de-Broglie wavelength of a charged particle accelerated from rest through a potential difference $V$ is given by:
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$

Given that $\lambda_p = \lambda_\alpha$, we have:
$\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_p q_p V_p}} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_\alpha q_\alpha V_\alpha}}$

Squaring both sides and rearranging the terms gives:
$m_p q_p V_p = m_\alpha q_\alpha V_\alpha$

We know that for an alpha particle, the mass is $m_\alpha = 4m_p$ and the charge is $q_\alpha = 2q_p$. Substituting these values into the equation:
$m_p q_p V_p = (4m_p)(2q_p)V_\alpha$
$V_p = 8V_\alpha$

Thus, the required ratio $\dfrac{V_p}{V_\alpha} = \dfrac{8}{1}$, or $8 : 1$.

Answer: $8 : 1$

107001.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
107001.text: What is the maximum covalency and the total number of valence orbitals, respectively, for a nitrogen atom?
107001.sol:
Nitrogen (atomic number $7$) belongs to the second period ($n=2$).

Its electronic configuration is $1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{3}$. The valence shell is the second shell, which contains one $2s$ orbital and three $2p$ orbitals. Thus, the total number of valence orbitals is $4$.

Because there are no $d$-orbitals in the second principal shell, nitrogen cannot expand its octet. Therefore, its maximum covalency is strictly limited to $4$ (for example, in the ammonium ion, $[NH_{4}]^{+}$).

Nitrogen has $5$ valence electrons and a common ground-state valency of $3$, but its maximum covalency is $4$.

Answer: $4$ and $4$

113886.subject: Chemistry
113886.text:
What mass of $\mathrm{KOH}$ is required to prepare $500 \mathrm{~mL}$ of an aqueous stock solution, if $20 \mathrm{~mL}$ of this solution exactly neutralizes $30 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $0.1 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{HNO}_{3}$?
(Molar mass of $\mathrm{KOH} = 56 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$)
113886.sol:
For the neutralization reaction between $\mathrm{KOH}$ and $\mathrm{HNO}_{3}$:
$\mathrm{M}_{1}\mathrm{V}_{1} = \mathrm{M}_{2}\mathrm{V}_{2}$
$\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{KOH}} \times 20 = 0.1 \times 30$
$\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{KOH}} = \dfrac{3}{20} = 0.15 \mathrm{M}$

Now, calculate the mass of $\mathrm{KOH}$ required for $500 \mathrm{~mL}$ ($0.5 \mathrm{~L}$) of this solution:
$\mathrm{Molarity} = \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Molar mass} \times \text{Volume (L)}}$
$0.15 = \dfrac{\mathrm{w}}{56 \times 0.5}$
$\mathrm{w} = 0.15 \times 56 \times 0.5 = 4.2 \mathrm{~g}$

Answer: $4.2 \mathrm{~g}$

114369.subject: Chemistry
114369.text:
The limiting molar conductivities ($\Lambda_m^\circ$) of three strong electrolytes are given below:

Electrolyte$\Lambda_m^\circ$ ($\text{S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$)
$\text{HNO}_3$$421$
$\text{KNO}_3$$145$
$\text{KA}$$104$


The molar conductivity of a $0.02\text{ M}$ solution of the weak acid $\text{HA}$ is $19\text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$. What is the dissociation constant ($K_a$) of the weak acid $\text{HA}$? (Assume $1 - \alpha \approx 1$)
114369.sol:
According to Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions:

$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HA}) = \Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HNO}_3) + \Lambda_m^\circ(\text{KA}) - \Lambda_m^\circ(\text{KNO}_3)$

$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HA}) = 421 + 104 - 145 = 380\text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$

The degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) is given by:

$\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ} = \dfrac{19}{380} = 0.05$

The dissociation constant ($K_a$) is calculated as:

$K_a = c\alpha^2$

$K_a = 0.02 \times (0.05)^2$

$K_a = 0.02 \times 0.0025 = 5.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Answer: $5.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ mol L}^{-1}$

121378.subject: Botany
121378.text: What type of genetic material do viruses that infect plants have?
121378.sol: In addition to proteins, viruses also contain genetic material, that could be either RNA or DNA. No virus contains both RNA and DNA. A virus is a nucleoprotein and the genetic material is infectious. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> In general, viruses that infect plants have single stranded RNA</mark>  and viruses that infect animals have either single or double stranded RNA or double stranded DNA.Bacterial viruses or bacteriophages (viruses that infect the bacteria) are usually double stranded DNA viruses. The protein coat called capsid made of small subunits called capsomeres, protects the nucleic acid. These capsomeres are arranged in helical or polyhedralgeometric forms. Viruses cause diseases like mumps, small pox, herpes and influenza. AIDS in humans is also caused by a virus. In plants, the symptoms can be mosaic formation, leaf rolling and curling, yellowing and vein clearing, dwarfing and stunted growth.

121554.text: Kingdom Fungi is divided into various classes based on the morphology of the mycelium, mode of spore formation, and fruiting bodies. Which of the following options correctly describes these three criteria for the members of class Phycomycetes?
options: Septate and branched mycelium, exogenous asexual spores, fruiting bodies absent

Septate and branched mycelium, endogenous asexual spores, basidiocarp present
Aseptate and coenocytic mycelium, endogenous asexual spores, fruiting bodies absent
121554.sol:
Kingdom Fungi is divided into classes based on mycelium morphology, mode of spore formation, and fruiting bodies.

For class Phycomycetes:
1. Morphology of mycelium: It is aseptate and coenocytic.
2. Mode of spore formation: Asexual spores (zoospores or aplanospores) are produced endogenously in a sporangium.
3. Fruiting bodies: They are absent in Phycomycetes (unlike Ascomycetes which form ascocarps and Basidiomycetes which form basidiocarps).

Thus, the correct description is aseptate and coenocytic mycelium, endogenous asexual spores, and absent fruiting bodies.

Answer: Aseptate and coenocytic mycelium, endogenous asexual spores, fruiting bodies absent

125670.subject: Botany
125670.text: To synthesise one molecule of glucose, a maize plant requires more energy than a tomato plant. How many additional ATP molecules are consumed by the maize plant for this process, and in which specific cells is this extra ATP utilised?
125670.sol:
Maize is a $\mathrm{C}_4$ plant, while tomato is a $\mathrm{C}_3$ plant.

In $\mathrm{C}_3$ plants, the synthesis of one glucose molecule requires $18 \text{ ATP}$ and $12 \text{ NADPH}$.

In $\mathrm{C}_4$ plants, the synthesis of one glucose molecule requires $30 \text{ ATP}$ and $12 \text{ NADPH}$. The additional $12 \text{ ATP}$ ($2 \text{ ATP}$ per $\mathrm{CO}_2$ molecule fixed) are required to regenerate phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) from pyruvate.

According to the $\mathrm{C}_4$ pathway (Hatch and Slack pathway), the regeneration of PEP takes place exclusively in the mesophyll cells.

Answer: $12 \text{ ATP}$, Mesophyll cells

126148.subject: Botany
126148.text:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological sequence regarding the development of a mature male gametophyte from a microspore mother cell (MMC) in a typical angiosperm:

I. Asymmetric mitotic division of the microspore nucleus.
II. Meiotic division of the microspore mother cell.
III. Dissociation of the microspore tetrad.
IV. Mitotic division of the generative cell to form two male gametes.
V. Formation of a large vegetative cell and a small generative cell.
126148.sol:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 6 - 7 | Paragraph: 1 - 2

The development of a mature male gametophyte from a microspore mother cell (MMC) in a typical angiosperm follows a specific sequence of events:

The microspore mother cell (MMC) first undergoes meiotic division to form a cluster of four cells called a microspore tetrad (Event II).

As the anther matures and dehydrates, the microspores dissociate from the tetrad and develop into individual pollen grains (Event III).

Inside the pollen grain, the microspore nucleus undergoes an asymmetric mitotic division (Event I).

This asymmetric division results in the formation of two unequal cells: a large vegetative cell and a small spindle-shaped generative cell (Event V).

Finally, the generative cell undergoes a second mitotic division to produce two non-motile male gametes, completing the formation of a mature three-celled male gametophyte (Event IV).

The correct chronological sequence is II $\rightarrow$ III $\rightarrow$ I $\rightarrow$ V $\rightarrow$ IV.

Answer: II $\rightarrow$ III $\rightarrow$ I $\rightarrow$ V $\rightarrow$ IV

127070.subject: Botany
127070.text:
Assertion : Presently, the global atmosphere is warming up.
Reason : The depletion of stratospheric ozone layer has resulted in increase in ultraviolet radiations reaching the earth.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
127070.sol:
The warming up of global atmosphere present day is due to the increase in green house effect.
Green house effect (GHE) describe the roles of water vapour, $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and other trace gases in keeping the Earth's surface warmer. These gases are relatively transparent to incoming shortwave radiation (visible spectrum), but are relatively opaque to outgoing reradiating (infrared rays) longwave radiation. The latter radiation, which would otherwise escape to space, is trapped by these gases within the lower levels of the atmosphere. The subsequent reradiation of some of the energy back to the surface maintains surface temperature higher than they would be if the gases were absent (without the green house effect the Earth's average global temperature would be -18 degree celsius rather than the present 15 degree celsius). There is concern that increasing concentration of the green house gases including $\mathrm{CO}_2, \mathrm{CH}_4$, and man made chlorofluorocarbons (CFCS), may enhance the green house effect and cause global warming.
Ozone layer present in the stratosphere is depleted by the aerosols and chloroflurocarbons. Ozone protects the earth from high energy ultra violet radiation.

127957.subject: Zoology
127957.text: In female frogs, where do the ureters and oviduct open separately?
127957.sol: The elimination of nitrogenous wastes is carried out by a well developed excretory system. The excretory system consists of a pair of kidneys, ureters, cloaca and urinary bladder. These are compact, dark red and bean like structures situated a little posteriorly in the body cavity on both sides of vertebral column. Each kidney is composed of several structural and functional units called uriniferous tubules or nephrons. Two ureters emerge from the kidneys in the male frogs. The ureters act as urinogenital duct which opens into the cloaca. In females the ureters and oviduct open seperately in the cloaca. The thin-walled urinary bladder is present ventral to the rectum which also opens in the cloaca. The frog excretes urea and thus is a ureotelic animal. Excretory wastes are carried by blood into the kidney where it is separated and excreted.

Assertion (A) is true as in all connective tissues except blood, the cells (like fibroblasts) secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

Reason (R) is also true as blood is a fluid connective tissue containing plasma, red blood cells (RBC), white blood cells (WBC) and platelets.

128135.sol:
In cockroaches, the primary excretory organs are the Malpighian tubules (A).

These are a ring of 100-150 yellow-coloured, thin filamentous structures located at the junction of the midgut (B) and hindgut (C).

The Malpighian tubules absorb nitrogenous waste from the haemolymph and convert it into uric acid, which is excreted out through the hindgut. Because it excretes uric acid, the cockroach is a uricotelic (D) insect.

Hepatic caeca are present at the junction of the foregut and midgut and are involved in secreting digestive juices, not excretion.

Answer: A - Malpighian tubules, B - midgut, C - hindgut, D - uricotelic

129917.subject: Zoology
129917.text: What are the specialised muscles involved in inspiration and expiration?
129917.sol: Breathing involves two stages : inspiration during which atmospheric air is drawn in and expiration by which the alveolar air is released out. The movement of air into and out of the lungs is carried out by creating a pressure gradient between the lungs and the atmosphere. Inspiration can occur if the pressure within the lungs (intra-pulmonary pressure) is less than the atmospheric pressure, i.e., there is a negative pressure in the lungs with respect to atmospheric pressure. Similarly, expiration takes place when the intra-pulmonary pressure is higher than the atmospheric pressure. The diaphragm and a specialised set of muscles – external and internal intercostals between the ribs, help in generation of such gradients. Inspiration is initiated by the contraction of diaphragm which increases the volume of thoracic chamber in the antero-posterior axis.

130789.text:
Read the following statements carefully:

(ii) Amniocentesis involves the analysis of the chromosomal pattern of cells in the amniotic fluid.

How many of the above statements are incorrect?
130789.sol:
Statement (i) is correct. 'Saheli' is a once-a-week oral contraceptive for females containing a non-steroidal preparation, developed by the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow.

Statement (ii) is correct. Amniocentesis is based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo.

Statement (iii) is incorrect. Amniocentesis is used to detect genetic disorders (such as Down syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anemia) by analysing foetal cells, not structural defects like cleft palate.

Statement (iv) is incorrect. The statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination was implemented to legally check the increasing menace of female foeticides, not the maternal mortality rate.

Therefore, exactly two statements are incorrect.

Answer: Two

131266.subject: Zoology
131266.text: A 52-year-old human female has experienced a permanent cessation of her menstrual cycle. Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding her current physiological state?
options: She has reached a stage termed as menopause
Her normal reproductive phase has ended
Her ovaries have largely depleted their stock of primary follicles
Cyclical ovarian changes will continue despite the absence of uterine bleeding
131266.sol:
In human females, the menstrual cycle ceases around 50 years of age, a stage termed as menopause. This marks the end of the normal reproductive phase.

By this age, the ovaries have largely depleted their finite stock of primary follicles. Because the follicles are depleted and unresponsive to gonadotropins, both the cyclical changes in the ovaries (follicular development and ovulation) and the corresponding changes in the uterus (menstruation) completely cease.

Therefore, the statement that cyclical ovarian changes will continue is incorrect.

Answer: Cyclical ovarian changes will continue despite the absence of uterine bleeding

132047.subject: Zoology
132047.text: What kind of traits did Mendel investigate in the garden pea plant?
132047.sol: During Mendel’s investigations into inheritance patterns it was for the first time that statistical analysis and mathematical logic were applied to problems in biology. His experiments had a large sampling size, which gave greater credibility to the data that he collected. Also, the confirmation of his inferences from experiments on successive generations of his test plants, proved that his results pointed to general rules of inheritance rather than being unsubstantiated ideas. Mendel investigated characters in the garden pea plant that were manifested as two opposing traits, e.g., tall or dwarf plants, yellow or green seeds. This allowed him to set up a basic framework of rules governing inheritance, which was expanded on by later scientists to account for all the diverse natural observations and the complexity inherent in them.

132121.subject: Zoology
132121.text: What was the phenotype of the F1 generation in the cross between true-breeding red-flowered and white-flowered snapdragons?
132121.sol: When experiments on peas were repeated using other traits in other plants, it was found that sometimes the F1 had a phenotype that did not resemble either of the two parents and was in between the two. The inheritance of flower colour in the dog flower (snapdragon or Antirrhinum sp.) is a good example to understand incomplete dominance. In a cross between true-breeding red-flowered (RR) and truebreeding white-flowered plants (rr), the F1 (Rr) was pink (Figure 4.6). When the F1 was self-pollinated the F2 resulted in the following ratio 1 (RR) Red: 2 (Rr) Pink: 1 (rr) White. Here the genotype ratios were exactly as we would expect in any mendelian monohybrid cross, but the phenotype ratios had changed from the 3:1 dominant : recessive ratio. What happened was that R was not completely dominant over r and this made it possible to distinguish Rr as pink from RR (red) and rr (white) .
